A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BrainSAIL and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Relocated implementation details and renumbered supplementary figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Tables 1–2, Section 4, and the appendices report original segmentation, fMRI prediction, semantic localization, and encoder-comparison results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds attribution-granularity case studies in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The frozen ViT backbones, voxel-wise encoders, dense attention adapters, and augmentation-averaging distillation remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Added statements about feature normalization and reusing the frozen voxel adapter clarify implementation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NSD and the ADE20k, COCO Object, COCO Stuff, and VOC20 segmentation benchmarks. The added natural-image attribution examples do not introduce a distinct dataset, population, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SCLIP and NACLIP as comparators, and the CLIP/DINO/SigLIP backbone comparisons are unchanged. Appendix A.2 reuses CLIP text probing already compared with brain relevance maps; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a four-image qualitative comparison using image-specific CLIP text prompts and S1 functional-region maps selected with t > 2, with cosine similarity for both probes. Existing splits, training settings, and Table 2's Pearson-based category assignment remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures S.1–S.2 investigate whether brain relevance maps preserve the fine semantic distinctions available in CLIP embeddings, including face/body overlap and misleading food-region attributions. These are additional diagnostic case studies; the earlier supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 7 retains standard-error bars across 100 images, and the appendix caveats about UMAP seed dependence remain unchanged. No additional run counts, uncertainty procedures, or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the matched pre-existing figures retain their quantitative results. Appendix A.2 adds qualitative findings that brain maps separate faces and bodies less consistently than CLIP text maps and can attribute food relevance to sunglasses or a pink dress.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and the derivation of averaging as the MSE-optimal embedding remain unchanged. Corrected coordinate-direction wording and added multi-view intuition do not alter the mathematical reasoning or introduce new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: learning-free feature distillation, semantic localization, joint brain-image factorization, feature correlates, and encoder comparisons. The rewritten abstract opening does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds specific qualifications: NSD co-occurrence may explain overlapping face/body maps, while size and saturation correlations may explain misleading food-region responses. Appendix A.1 also expands the mechanism explanation by treating augmentation-dependent artifacts as measurement noise.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code repository link and documents native-space fMRI files, nsdgeneral masking, selection of 45 of 180 HCP regions by noise ceiling, and exclusion of V1–V4. It also explicitly states dense-feature normalization. These are additional disclosures; the existing training and extraction settings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Adeli et al. (2023), Yeung et al. (2024), Shirakawa et al. (2024), Kobayashi et al. (2022), and Mildenhall et al. (2021). The main positioning addition relates learning-free distillation to gradient-based NeRF and feature-field methods, while retaining the broader research framing.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract opening, refines terminology and explanations, adds distillation intuition, and moves implementation details from Appendix A.9 to A.1. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds two composite appendix figures, labels Figure 7's axis as Spearman correlation, refines captions, and relocates several figures and tables. The existing supplementary displays are retained and renumbered, with the overall visual design preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through explicit fMRI processing and voxel-selection details plus a code link, and improves interpretive transparency through concrete attribution failures in Appendix A.2. These address specific omissions in v1 while preserving its quantitative evidence. The gains remain limited because the new cases are qualitative and their proposed causes are not experimentally isolated.
